Maria: Heads-up — ran a quick HF->Redwood tokenizer conversion for the new sparse-embedding model and seeing weird ID gaps when serializing added_tokens.json :thinking_face:
Jeff: show me an example?
Maria: minimal repro: I loaded the HF tokenizer, called tokenizer.add_tokens(['<SPECIAL_A>', '<SPECIAL_B>']) then saved. When Redwood import reads added_tokens.json the IDs are offset by +2 compared to HF's convert_tokens_to_ids output.
Sasha: do you have the exact commands and a snippet of the saved added_tokens.json?
Maria: yup — commands: `tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("hf/sparse-100m")
new_ids = tok.add_tokens(["<SPECIAL_A>", "<SPECIAL_B>"])
tok.save_pretrained("./work/tokenizer")`
Maria: saved added_tokens.json: `[{"id":50256,"special_token":"<SPECIAL_A>"},{"id":50257,"special_token":"<SPECIAL_B>"}]`
Maria: but `tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<SPECIAL_A>","<SPECIAL_B>"])` returns `[50254, 50255]` locally. Import shows 50256/50257, so downstream model outputs map incorrectly. :eyes:
Jeff: that smells like a BOS/EOS/PAD insertion during Redwood's loading pipeline. Do we shift token IDs to reserve 0..n for special tokens?
Sasha: Redwood import does consult config.json special tokens and also looks for pad/bos/eos/unk. If HF tokenizer has different special_token mappings than the config, import may remap and write a normalized added_tokens.json.
Sam: can you paste the model config.json? particularly fields `bos_token_id`, `eos_token_id`, `pad_token_id`, `additional_special_tokens`?
Maria: config.json excerpt: `"bos_token_id": 0, "eos_token_id": 1, "pad_token_id": null, "unk_token_id": 2, "additional_special_tokens": ["<SPECIAL_A>", "<SPECIAL_B>"]`
Jeff: aha — pad_token_id null but bos/eos/unk occupy low ids. HF tokenizer add_tokens returns absolute ids into the vocab, but Redwood import canonicalizes special ids (it ensures bos/eos/unk are mapped to reserved IDs 0/1/2) and then rewrites added_tokens.json with adjusted ids. If your downstream code assumed HF's absolute ids, you'll get a mismatch.
Sasha: workaround: when converting, run the HF tokenizer through `tokenizer.special_tokens_map` -> reconcile with config.json, then call `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)`, and verify `tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(id)` matches the saved mapping.
Maria: trying that now. Also noticed chat template serialization inserts a `<|pad|>` token into the system prompt which wasn't present originally, shifting all subsequent special token positions in some templates. That's possibly why ids jump by +2 in my case.
Sam: good catch — chat templates that prepend BOS/PAD will change effective vocabulary indices if loader assumes template tokens are in vocab and reserves ids. We should avoid implicit template tokens during token-id reconciliation.
TokenBot: Incident created: TKT-8342 — "HF->Redwood token id skew on added_tokens.json when config special tokens differ" assigned to eng-ml.
Jeff: short-term fix: add an import-time check that compares `converted_ids = [tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(t) for t in additional_special_tokens]` to `added_tokens.json` ids; if mismatch, emit a warning and a migration map file `token_id_map.json` for runtime remapping.
Maria: that warning saved me — I patched the loader to output a map and updated the model card. After runtime remap, outputs align and eval BLEU/embeddings are stable.
Sasha: let's add a small test to our onboarding checklist: 1) ensure config.json special ids explicit (no nulls), 2) run `hf_tokenizer_roundtrip_check.py` that verifies token->id->token identity for all special tokens and added_tokens.json, 3) fail onboarding if drift > 0.
Sam: +1. Also add a note to docs about chat templates possibly injecting pad/bos tokens during serialization.
Maria: thanks all — leaving the incident with repro and patch in TKT-8342. Will follow up with a PR for the loader warnings. :thumbsup:
